tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Geodesics Dx, Dy from far-apart points do not meet] Let initial sub-geodesics of $D_x$ and $D_y$ have a common final endpoint and otherwise be disjoint. Their union separates $A$ with one disk component $B$; then $B\cap c_0$ contains no arc of length one.
Proof

↗ lem:no-geodesic-spans-c0-to-c0 \sketch Repeat the maximal-focusing argument in $B$. The non-$c_0$ part of its boundary has length below $0.2$, while final radial endpoints cover length at least $0.86$, forcing a radial with both endpoints on $c_0$.

□

Corollary
[Short arcs with meeting geodesics bound a focusing disk]
